newsitem.title: USA: Explosion at Shell plant near Houston.
newsitem.headline: Explosion at Shell plant near Houston.

text.p: A powerful explosion and fire ripped through a Shell Oil Co plant near Houston on Sunday but no one was seriously injured, police said.

The explosion occurred shortly after 10:00 a.m. CDT/1500 GMT in the petrochemical section of the plant in the Houston suburb of Deer Park and local residents were told to turn off their air conditioners, close all doors and windows and stay inside.
The plant produces ethylene and propylene, which are extremely flammable feedstocks for other chemical products, but company officials said the danger had passed.

"The fire is contained. We have industrial hygienists in the area and they are not detecting any levels of toxins outside the plant," Lynn Elsenhans, president and chief executive officer of the Deer Park plant, told Reuters.

"Everyone has been accounted for and there are no serious injuries," Elsenhans said. She said one employee was taken to the hospital with chest pains but it was not clear whether they were linked to the blast.
The cause of the explosion was under investigation.
A Deer Park police dispatcher also said there were no injuries but that the blast rocked nearby homes and businesses.
"There were a lot of businesses on the south side of Interstate 225 that had a lot of damage. A lot of windows were blown out," she said.
One local resident, Ray Smith, said the explosion shook his house and woke him up. "I didn't hear a boom or anything but, man, it really rattled my house."
Police closed the highway after the explosion and told residents to the north to stay inside.
Shell Oil is a unit of Anglo-Dutch oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
